newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares advance in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares advance in cautious trade.

text.p: Oil shares advanced in cautious Nigerian trade on Wednesday amid continuing fears of dwindling profits, traders said.
But the all-share index fell to 6,618.8.35 from 6,623.78 on blue chip losses.
Total closed at 49.25 naira, a gain of 10 kobo, similar to that made by most other oil marketers. Mobil was 41.95 naira, Texaco was 28.00 naira and Unipetrol closed at 44.50 naira.
Analysts forecast oil firms would be hit by the tight profit margins allowed them by government and product scarcity caused by frequent breakdowns at Nigeria's four petroleum refineries.
Wednesday's best finishers were construction firms as investors took profit from highly-priced stocks to raise their stake in cheaper securities.
Cappa and D'Alberto rose by 20 kobo to 8.80 naira while G. Cappa was 9.30 naira, up 25 kobo.
National Salt Company rose 25 kobo, the maximum five percent allowed daily to 5.30 naira, also on keen investor interest.
On the strength of its good seven-month result announced on Tuesday, Union Dicon Salt garnered 20 kobo to 37.70 naira.
Nigerian Breweries shed 50 kobo in its continuing slide to end at 10.50 naira. One dealer said investors were still selling large volumes of the company's stock.
Conglomerate John Holt was down 10 kobo at 10.20 naira, the same as First Aluminium at 4.40 naira.

Cement companies ended mixed. West African Portland notched 20 kobo to reach 36.70 naira, its highest this year while Ashaka Cement lost some of the grounds it made earlier this week, ending five down at 19.20 naira as did Afribank at 5.05 naira.
